problems.title: Stack contents
problems.statement: Same input, next-greater stack of indices (values non-increasing).

parts.prompt: Stack size just before processing index 4 (72)?

problems.solution: Before 72 the stack holds indices 1, 2, 3 (71, 69, 68); 72 pops all three.

problems.title: Amortised
problems.solution: At most n each: O(n) total even though one while loop can pop many.

parts.prompt: Which bar is the shortest in the best rectangle?

problems.title: Contribution counting
problems.statement: a = [3, 1, 2, 4]: for each element, the number of subarrays in which it's the minimum (ties: previous strictly smaller, next smaller-or-equal).

problems.title: Ties
problems.statement: Why break ties asymmetrically (strict on one side)?

options: So subarrays whose minimum appears twice are counted once

problems.solution: In [2, 2] the subarray [2, 2] has two equal minima; symmetric strict rules would count it zero times, symmetric non-strict twice.

problems.title: Previous smaller
problems.statement: For each element, the index of the previous strictly smaller element (−1 if none), for [4, 2, 5, 3, 3, 1].
hints: Read the stack top after popping ≥ elements.
problems.solution: Index 3: previous smaller is 2 at index 1; index 4: the earlier 3 isn't strictly smaller, so 1; index 5: none.

problems.title: Which primitive?
problems.statement: Stock span: for each day, the number of consecutive days up to today with price ≤ today's.

parts.prompt: Span on the last day of [100, 80, 60, 70, 60, 75, 85]?

problems.solution: Previous greater of 85 is 100 at index 0: span 6 − 0 = 6.
